Q: How to Migrate from Java 8 32-bit to Java 17 32-bit? Eclipse Support Issues A:

Java 17

no 32-bit version of Java 17 available

Incorrect.

Implementations of the Java specifications are available from several vendors including:

  • Amazon
  • Microsoft
  • Azul Systems
  • Oracle
  • IBM
  • Red Hat
  • Adoptium of the Eclipse Foundation
  • BellSoft
  • SAP
  • … and more

Some of those release 32-bit products for Java 17.

For example:

  • Adoptium provides a JDK and a JRE implementing Java 17 specs for 32-bit Windows.
  • Azul Systems provides a JDK and a JRE, both optionally bundled with the OpenJFX implementation of JavaFX, implementing Java 17 specs for 32-bit Windows and 32-bit Linux.

Java 24

The OpenJDK project dropped specifically the Windows OS 32-bit x86 platform.

See JEP 479: Remove the Windows 32-bit x86 Port.

Java 25

The OpenJDK project removed all code paths that apply only to 32-bit x86 in Java 25.

See JEP 503: Remove the 32-bit x86 Port.

Q: What does a template return? A:

You lied. You called a template with two different types, when the stencil says it wants a single type.

You called it as max(int, double). The compiler may try to be nice and convert the double to int, or there is a possibility you meant to call max<double>(double, double). Now you're giving the compiler a headache.

FYI, 4.2 is default double. If you want float, add the f suffix, such as 4.2f.

To answer the title of your question, a function template returns whatever the return type is.

Q: git stash failed when trying to perform a git pull A:

The error fatal: stash failed indicates that an operation akin to git stash was attempted.

There is a configuration option pull.autoStash. It looks like this is enabled in this repository.

If that is the case, you can temporarily disable the option with

git pull --no-autostash origin master

This may still fail, but this time because there are uncommitted modifications in the worktree. The real solution is then, of course, to handle the uncommitted changes, i.e., either to commit them or to discard them.
